In compliance with the JAR Data Policy, I provide the following information regarding the data

evidence.description: Author describes collecting SEC Exhibit 10 material from 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K filings during 1994–2017 and the content filters applied.
evidence.file: Zhu datasheet.pdf
evidence.quote:
1. I started to collect the URLs of all Exhibit 10s of SEC forms 10‐K, 10‐Q, and 8‐K filed
       between January 1994 and December 2017 using the SEC Analytics Suite, and
       downloaded Exhibit 10s from EDGAR by using Python in May 2018. I then restricted
       Exhibit 10s to these containing the terms, “Credit Agreement”, “Loan Agreement”, or
       “Loan and Security Agreement”; “GAAP” or “Generally Accepted Accounting
       Principles”; and “financial covenants” or “negative covenants”. I extracted GAAP
       provisions from each loan contract and identify GAAP provision types.

evidence.description: Author names Compustat, CRSP, DealScan, and Mergent FISD as financial data sources.
evidence.file: Zhu datasheet.pdf
evidence.quote:
2. I started to collect financial data from Compustat, stock return data from CRSP, data on
       loan contract characteristics from DealScan, and data on bond ratings from Mergent FISD
       in August 2018.

evidence.description: Author describes covenant-violation data periods, procedures, and exclusions.
evidence.file: Zhu datasheet.pdf
evidence.quote:
3. Covenant violation data between June 1996 and December 2007 are from Roberts and
       Sufi [2009b] who share the URLs of 10-K/Qs that disclose violations. I collected covenant
       violation data from January 2008 to December 2017 by modifying the procedures
       prescribed by Nini et al. [2012] in November 2018. To enhance the probability of
       capturing violations triggered by accounting changes, in October, November, and
       December 2021, I reviewed the data and excluded violations of capital expenditure and
       M&A covenants.

evidence.description: Author describes 448 amended loan contracts and the sources used to collect them.
evidence.file: Zhu datasheet.pdf
evidence.quote:
4. 448 amended loan contracts that were adjusted for the effect of specific accounting
       changes on financial covenants were collected in January, February, and March 2022. I
       collected these contracts from three sources: (i) amended contracts with a complete loan
       path covered by EDGAR, (ii) borrowers’ summary of contract amendments in Item 1.01
       of 8-Ks—Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement, and (iii) lenders’ comments on
       contract amendments reported to the Thomson Reuters LPC’ LoanConnector database.

dependency_review.description: Three form-specific SEC Exhibit 10 tables are external inputs to the supplied stack and belong to the shared filing-text requirement.
THESIS.EXHIBIT10 is assembled and filtered from the three form-specific inputs; retain it as a generated intermediate.
The code reads THESIS.EXHIBIT10_GAAP before its later in-place transformations, so the initial author-coded table is a required input.
The FYEAR_SIC lookup is joined to the GAAP sample and is treated as an annual Compustat-derived input with unresolved SIC mapping.
The DealScan facility table is filtered and joined to the contract sample; the common facility candidate is schema evidence only.
The DealScan–Compustat linking table supplies FACID, GVKEY, and FIC for the USA filter; its compatible product and producer remain unresolved.
THESIS.GVKEY_QUARTER is the input to the quarterly lag/lead expansion and requires quarterly Compustat history.
THESIS.GVKEY_QUARTER_4 is produced by PROC EXPAND from GVKEY_QUARTER with four lags and four leads.
The annual Model 1 control table is read and transformed using Compustat variables before it is joined to the GAAP sample.
THESIS.EXHIBIT10_GAAP_MODEL1 is constructed by joining the GAAP sample and annual controls, then subsequent controls are added.
The facility-to-lender input is read to construct lender counts; the common LENDERSHARES candidate has not been mapped to this author table.
The author-side LENDER table supplies lender identity and arranger fields used in the reputation construction.
The author-side 1990–2021 facility history is filtered to U.S. and United States Dollar facilities before annual reputation counts.
THESIS.LENDER_REPUTATION is generated from lender and historical facility inputs and ranked by year.
The annual accounting-change count is joined as a control variable and requires its author-defined year/count input.
The most-recent 10-K WORDCOUNT table is an external SEC Analytics Suite input keyed to GVKEY and fiscal year.
Monthly returns are an external input to the rolling return-window and volatility construction.
THESIS.MONTHLY_RETURN_STD is generated from monthly return data with 36 lagged returns and date-valid CCM joins.
The dated THESIS.MODEL2_CRSP_20220124 panel is read as an input; its producer and source-data contract are not in the supplied program.
THESIS.MODEL2_CRSP is transformed from the dated CRSP input, joined to CCM and quarterly keys, and used to construct return signs.
THESIS.MODEL2_CRSP_POSITIVE is a generated positive-return branch of MODEL2_CRSP.
Hand-collected covenant violations are a required external input to the positive and negative return branches.
The package-level probability-of-violation input is externally supplied to the positive-return branch.
Quarterly Compustat inputs are read and transformed into the Model 2 quarterly controls.
The author-side dividend table supplies DVT by GVKEY and fiscal year for the Model 2 branch.
THESIS.MODEL2_CRSP_NEGATIVE is the generated negative-return branch retained by the supplied program.
The author-side bond-rating panel is read before its rating-type and 1996–2017 date filters.
THESIS.MODEL2_FISD is generated from the prepared rating panel and linked through the bond–CRSP and CRSP–Compustat tables.
THESIS.MODEL2_FISD_UPGRADE is a generated rating-upgrade branch.
THESIS.MODEL2_FISD_DOWNGRADE is a generated rating-downgrade branch.

review_notes: The assessed target is the supplied SAS data-preparation program. The datasheet also mentions Python/SAS/Stata analyses, but this archive contains no later analysis driver; the packaged one-column facility-ID DTA is not an analysis panel, so no separate analysis-only scope is supported.

The author states that no data were obtained from an organization on a proprietary basis and separately notes that hand-collected datasets were not publicly available. This assessment does not infer current-user access or licensing status from either statement and does not independently reconstruct hand-collected inputs.

Common catalog candidates and successful bounded probes establish product-file candidates and selected schema fields only. They do not establish full-population or historical coverage, author-table mapping, or current entitlement. The authorized same-catalog COMP.FUNDA SICH/INDFMT probe is retained as a candidate; it is not asserted to be equivalent to the source's SIC/FYEAR_SIC input. The exact SIC request failure is preserved in probes/catalog_probe_capture_comp_funda_sic.json.

The exact FISD.MERGEDISSUE one-row reader timed out after its 15-second bound. Its failure is preserved in probes/catalog_probe_capture_001.json. The ratings sample and issue metadata/timeout remain possible upstream support under R_FISD_PREPARED_PANEL, not separate mandatory visible raw inputs; no raw-to-prepared construction or full coverage is verified. The SEC raw, parsed, and LM10X checks were directory-metadata checks with no listing or coverage verification.

The SAS credential-screened ranges [[20,21],[27,147],[606,610],[621,622]] remain wholly opaque. Screening/redaction helpers and outputs are retained. E_SOURCE_SCREEN_PROCESS, E_ENVIRONMENT_PROCESS, and E_WORKER_PROCESS_TRACE are process-only evidence rows and are intentionally unreferenced by every scientific evidence_ids list. No credentials, connection defaults, or raw candidate lines are reproduced.

The source's nvalues_new filter at line 904 follows a visible nvalues count at lines 887–889; no nvalues_new assignment appears in the safely reviewed source. An imported monthly-return field remains possible, so this is a conditional contract issue and no source change was proposed or applied.

All 35 frozen dependency IDs are reviewed once; D0021 and D0033 now map separately to the supplied MODEL2_CRSP_20220124 and MODEL3_CRSP_MONTHLY input panels. The literal-free source structure scan also identified CIK/GVKEY, CCM, and WRDSAPPS bond-link reads outside that frozen list, represented as requirements without inventing dependency IDs. Generated panel/branch tables remain distinct from imported inputs.

The first incremental draft and source-close snapshot are preserved. A first capture-wrapper path error temporarily merged the old partial draft; the resulting checkpoint is retained, the working draft was reset from the template, and the expanded draft was rebuilt in captured sections. A merger that assumed an id key failed before writing; its exact captured failure is preserved, and the versioned merger handled dependency_id/dependency_ids. No faulty helper was deleted or overwritten.

The supplied program requires Base SAS and SAS/ETS PROC EXPAND and calls %winsor. SAS initialization/product availability and the %winsor definition remain unverified. No SAS executable, author-code compile/parser/syntax run, model, regression, installation, or data payload download was run during this assessment.
The only web checks were official static SEC and SAS documentation pages; no filing, data, archive, or document payload was requested or followed.
The author’s nonproprietary-data statement is quoted in E_DOC_NONPROPRIETARY and is not treated as proof of current-user access or entitlement.
